nodes.name: HTTP entry and GraphQL view
nodes.summary: Django URL table, the GraphQL view that answers GET with the playground and POST with queries or batches, and the small helper views.
nodes.detail: Uvicorn serves the ASGI (Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface) application; Django resolves the path through saleor/urls.py. The single GraphQL door is GraphQLView, mounted at /graphql/ with Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) checks disabled. Plugin webhook routes and the thumbnail and image routes hand off to other areas' views. The JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) route publishes the public signing key, and in DEBUG mode the static, media and home routes are added.

nodes.name: HTTP routes
nodes.summary: Every route declared in saleor/urls.py, one box per method.
nodes.detail: Routes are declared with re_path regular expressions; the ids here use the normalised path. GET and POST are listed for the plugin routes because the Django views accept any method.

nodes.name: ASGI server stack
nodes.summary: The Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (ASGI) application and the wrappers around Django: health check, gzip, CORS, telemetry and usage telemetry.
nodes.detail: saleor/asgi/__init__.py builds the callable Uvicorn loads: Django's patched ASGI handler, wrapped in order by the /health/ shortcut, gzip compression, the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) handler, the telemetry wrapper that tags spans with the request host, and, when SEND_USAGE_TELEMETRY is true, a lifespan hook that reports anonymous usage once a day. preload_app() initialises OpenTelemetry, imports the URL table and freezes the garbage collector so forked workers share memory.

nodes.name: Schema assembly
nodes.summary: Builds the one GraphQL schema from every module's Query and Mutation classes, adds Apollo Federation fields, prints the SDL and patches the GraphQL runtime.
nodes.detail: api.py imports the Queries and Mutations mix-ins of each domain module (account, checkout, order, product and the rest) and combines them into Query and Mutation classes by multiple inheritance. build_federated_schema() turns them into a graphene Schema and adds the _entities and _service fields for Apollo Federation. Deprecated fields and fields marked monitor_usage get a wrapper that records a usage metric. The cached backend parses and validates each document string once and keeps up to 1000 parsed documents in a least-recently-used dictionary.

nodes.name: Query limits and guards
nodes.summary: The checks a document passes before it runs: query cost, alias and mutation counts, introspection mixing, subscriptions, storefront traffic and upload validation.
nodes.detail: After parsing, the view rejects documents that mix introspection with data queries and any subscription operation. validate_query() then runs three graphql-core validation rules in one pass: the cost validator driven by COST_MAP, the alias count limit and the mutation count limit. Errors are only enforced when GRAPHQL_QUERY_MAX_COMPLEXITY is non-zero. Just before execution the storefront traffic guard returns HTTP 401 for anonymous and customer requests when the shop has disabled direct storefront traffic.

nodes.name: Error handling
nodes.summary: How failures come back: GraphQL errors formatted with an exception code, internal messages masked outside DEBUG, typed mutation errors and reference-cycle cleanup.
nodes.detail: Execution errors are formatted by format_error(): the original exception is unwrapped, logged as handled or unhandled, and its message replaced by 'Internal Server Error' unless it is an allowed type or DEBUG is on. Mutations do not raise for validation problems; BaseMutation turns Django ValidationError into a list of typed error objects with field, message and code. The view returns 400 for invalid documents, 413 for oversized bodies and 401 for blocked storefront traffic.

nodes.name: Request context and authentication
nodes.summary: Builds the per-request GraphQL context: the app or user behind the token, JSON Web Token (JWT) signing and decoding, the refresh-token cookie and resolver permission decorators.
nodes.detail: get_context_value() decorates the Django request with a dataloader cache, the replica flag, the calling app (from an app token) and a lazy user. The user is resolved on first access through Django's authentication backends: JSONWebTokenBackend decodes a Saleor JSON Web Token (JWT) and checks the user's token key, PluginBackend lets plugins authenticate. JWTManager signs tokens with RS256 using RSA_PRIVATE_KEY and serves the public key as a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS). Resolvers are guarded by permission decorators and PermissionsField, which call the permission module.

nodes.name: URL table
nodes.summary: Django URL patterns: the GraphQL view, three plugin webhook routes, thumbnails, original images, the JWKS document and, in DEBUG, static, media and home.
nodes.detail: Mounts GraphQLView.as_view(backend=backend, schema=schema) at ^graphql/$ wrapped in csrf_exempt. Plugin routes accept a plugin id and optionally a channel slug and forward to saleor/plugins/views.py. The thumbnail route takes an instance id, a size and an optional format. When DEBUG is true it appends /media/ served by serve_media_view, /static/ served by Django's staticfiles view and the home page at the root.
facts: Static, media and home routes exist only when DEBUG is true

nodes.summary: Renders templates/home/index.html with links to the storefront and dashboard, added only when DEBUG is true.

nodes.name: GraphQL view
nodes.summary: GraphQLView: Saleor's own replacement for graphene-django's view, adding the playground, multipart file upload, batching, tracing, metrics, cost reporting and an introspection cache.
nodes.detail: dispatch() routes GET to the playground and POST to handle_query(); other methods get 405. handle_query() opens a server span and request metrics, then _handle_query() parses the body and runs one operation or a batch. execute_graphql_request() parses through the cached backend, rejects mixed introspection and subscriptions, computes the query cost, builds the context, applies the storefront traffic guard and executes. Introspection-only results are cached in Django's cache under a key made of the Saleor version and a SHA-256 of the query when DEBUG is off.
facts: Requests slower than GRAPHQL_SPANS_MARK_SLOW_AFTER (30 seconds) mark the span as an error
GRAPHQL_CACHE_SUFFIX is appended to the introspection cache key when set

nodes.name: GraphQLView
nodes.summary: The Django class-based view mounted at /graphql/; holds the schema, backend and GraphQL middleware list.
nodes.detail: Built once by urls.py with the cached backend and schema from api.py. GRAPHQL_MIDDLEWARE names are imported and instantiated in __init__. HANDLED_EXCEPTIONS (GraphQLError, PyJWTError, PermissionDenied, InvalidIPAddress) decide whether a failure is logged as handled or unhandled.

nodes.name: GraphQLView.dispatch()
nodes.summary: Routes GET to the playground (or 405 when PLAYGROUND_ENABLED is false) and POST to handle_query().
nodes.detail: Wrapped by the observability report_view decorator from the webhooks area, which buffers API call reports for apps subscribed to observability events.

nodes.name: GraphQLView.handle_query()
nodes.summary: Entry point for every POST /graphql/: wraps the request in a server tracing span and request metrics, then delegates to _handle_query().
nodes.detail: Extracts the incoming trace context from headers, records method, URL, user agent and accepted encoding on the span, and injects trace context into the response headers. After the response it records request count and duration, reports the call to observability buffers and marks the span as an error when the request took longer than GRAPHQL_SPANS_MARK_SLOW_AFTER seconds.

nodes.name: GraphQLView._handle_query()
nodes.summary: Parses the body and runs a single operation or a batch list, returning the worst status code of the batch.
nodes.detail: parse_body() accepts application/graphql, application/json (an object or a list), form and multipart bodies. RequestDataTooBig returns 413 and an unparsable body 400. A list longer than GRAPHQL_BATCH_MAX_COUNT is rejected with 400 before anything runs; each entry goes through get_response() and the response status is the maximum of the entries.

nodes.name: GraphQLView.get_response()
nodes.summary: Turns an ExecutionResult into the response dictionary: formatted errors, data, extensions, and the status code (400 when invalid, 401 when storefront traffic is blocked).
nodes.signature: def get_response(self, request, data) -> tuple[GraphQLOperationResult | None, int]

nodes.name: GraphQLView.execute_graphql_request()
nodes.summary: Runs one operation: parse, introspection check, subscription rejection, cost and count validation, context, storefront guard, cache lookup and execution.
nodes.detail: Each failure path records the operation count and cost metrics with an error type and returns an invalid ExecutionResult. The query identifier (sorted root field names) and an MD5 fingerprint label the span. Cost errors are returned only when GRAPHQL_QUERY_MAX_COMPLEXITY is set; the computed cost is added to the result extensions. Exceptions during execution are caught; integer overflow and ValueError are turned into GraphQLError. The context's dataloaders are cleared in a finally block.
nodes.signature: def execute_graphql_request(self, request: HttpRequest, data: dict) -> ExecutionResult
nodes.code:
query_cost, cost_errors = validate_query(
                schema=schema,
                document_ast=document.document_ast,
                variables=variables,
                cost_map=COST_MAP,
            )
            span.set_attribute(saleor_attributes.GRAPHQL_OPERATION_COST, query_cost)

            if settings.GRAPHQL_QUERY_MAX_COMPLEXITY and cost_errors:
                result = ExecutionResult(errors=cost_errors, invalid=True)
                error_description = self.format_span_error_description(result)
                span.set_status(status=StatusCode.ERROR, description=error_description)
                error_type = cost_errors[0].__class__.__name__ if cost_errors else None

nodes.name: Helper views
nodes.summary: Three small Django views: the DEBUG home page, the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) document and the DEBUG-only media file server.
nodes.detail: jwks() returns the JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) from the configured JWT manager. home() renders links taken from the STOREFRONT_URL and DASHBOARD_URL environment variables. serve_media_view() refuses with 404 when DEBUG is off and forces Content-Disposition: attachment on local media files.

nodes.name: jwks()
nodes.summary: Returns get_jwt_manager().get_jwks() as JSON for GET /.well-known/jwks.json.

nodes.name: home()
nodes.summary: Renders the DEBUG landing page with storefront and dashboard links from environment variables.

nodes.name: Playground page
nodes.summary: HTML page that loads the GraphQL Playground explorer pointed at the API URL and plugins URL passed by the view.

nodes.name: ASGI application
nodes.summary: Builds the Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (ASGI) callable Uvicorn serves, stacking health check, gzip, CORS, telemetry and usage telemetry around Django.
nodes.detail: The stack is applied inside out: get_asgi_application() first, then health_check('/health/'), gzip_compression, cors_handler and telemetry_middleware; usage_telemetry_middleware is added only when SEND_USAGE_TELEMETRY is true. preload_app() calls initialize_telemetry(), forces the URL resolver to import every view and runs gc.freeze().
facts: The Dockerfile starts uvicorn saleor.asgi:application with 2 workers on port 8000

nodes.name: PatchedASGIHandler
nodes.summary: Django's ASGIHandler with a copied handle() that clears its task list after each request to break a reference cycle (Django ticket 36700).
nodes.detail: Reads the body, creates the request, runs the response and a disconnect listener as two tasks, cancels whichever is still pending and clears the list so the RequestAborted traceback does not keep the tasks alive.

nodes.name: health_check()
nodes.summary: ASGI wrapper that answers GET /health/ with an empty 200 text/plain response without touching Django or the database.

nodes.name: cors_handler()
nodes.summary: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) wrapper: answers OPTIONS preflights and adds allow-origin headers when the Origin matches ALLOWED_GRAPHQL_ORIGINS.
nodes.detail: Origins are matched with fnmatchcase against each pattern in ALLOWED_GRAPHQL_ORIGINS (default '*'). Preflight answers 200 when matched and 400 otherwise, allowing POST and OPTIONS, a fixed header list including Authorization-Bearer and Source-Service-Name, and a max age of 600 seconds. For other requests it rewrites the response start message to add credentials, the echoed origin and Vary: Origin.

nodes.name: Usage telemetry reporter
nodes.summary: On ASGI lifespan startup, sends anonymous instance statistics (version and object counts) to Saleor's usage telemetry endpoint at most once per SEND_USAGE_TELEMETRY_AFTER_TIMEDELTA.
nodes.detail: usage_telemetry_middleware() listens for lifespan.startup and schedules send_usage_telemetry_task(), which sleeps 0 to 5 seconds to spread workers, checks SiteSettings.usage_telemetry_reported_at, marks it, gathers counts from the replica and POSTs JSON with a SHA-256 content header through the hardened HTTP client. On failure it resets the timestamp so the next start retries.

nodes.name: Schema root (api.py)
nodes.summary: Assembles the public GraphQL schema: Query, Mutation and Subscription classes, the @doc and @webhookEventsInfo directives, extra types and the cached validating backend.
nodes.detail: Query inherits 22 domain Queries mix-ins and Mutation 24 Mutations mix-ins. build_federated_schema() receives unit enums, webhook subscription payload types, payment and attribute extra types, and the Subscription root used only for webhook subscription documents. monitor_fields_usage() then wraps tracked resolvers. API_PATH is the lazily reversed URL of the 'api' route.
facts: Translations contribute queries only; translate mutations are registered by each domain's schema

nodes.name: Query root
nodes.summary: The root Query type: the union of every domain module's Queries class by multiple inheritance.

nodes.name: Mutation root
nodes.summary: The root Mutation type: the union of every domain module's Mutations class, including metadata, shop and external notifications.

nodes.name: SaleorGraphQLBackend
nodes.summary: graphql-core backend that parses and validates eagerly, so the cached document either executes directly or returns the stored validation errors.
nodes.detail: Validation errors produce a GraphQLDocument whose execute is a partial of _fail(), returning an invalid ExecutionResult. The module-level backend wraps it in GraphQLCachedBackend with CacheDict(1000), a least-recently-used dictionary keyed by the document string.
nodes.code:
document_ast = parse(document_string)
        validation_errors = validate(schema, document_ast)
        if validation_errors:
            return GraphQLDocument(
                schema=schema,
                document_string=document_string,
                document_ast=document_ast,
                execute=partial(_fail, validation_errors),
            )

        return GraphQLDocument(
            schema=schema,
            document_string=document_string,
            document_ast=document_ast,
            execute=partial(execute, schema, document_ast, **self.execute_params),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
facts: Up to 1000 parsed documents are cached per process

nodes.name: Apollo Federation support
nodes.summary: Adds Apollo Federation to the schema: the _Any scalar, the _Entity union, and the _entities and _service fields on Query.
nodes.detail: Types decorated with federated_entity(key_fields) register themselves; resolve_entities() validates each representation's __typename and fields, batches them per type and calls the type's resolve_references. FEDERATED_QUERY_MAX_ENTITIES (default 100) caps representations per query because the protocol has no limit of its own. _service returns the printed schema without subscriptions and without the schema block.
facts: FEDERATED_QUERY_MAX_ENTITIES defaults to 100; 0 disables the cap

nodes.name: resolve_entities()
nodes.summary: Resolves federation representations in batches per type after checking the entity limit, __typename and known fields.

nodes.name: Core queries and file upload
nodes.summary: CoreQueries exposes the deprecated taxTypes list from the plugin manager; CoreMutations exposes fileUpload.
nodes.detail: taxTypes asks the plugin manager for tax rate type choices; it is deprecated in favour of taxClasses.

nodes.name: Schema printer
nodes.summary: Prints the schema as SDL including Saleor's @doc categories and @webhookEventsInfo directives, for schema.graphql and the federation _service field.
nodes.detail: print_schema() filters out introspection and built-in scalar types and prints object directives for doc categories. The get_graphql_schema management command writes its output to stdout.

nodes.name: Committed schema SDL
nodes.summary: The generated public GraphQL schema; regenerated with `poe build-schema` and checked in so continuous integration catches stale changes.
nodes.detail: AGENTS.md requires new fields to carry ADDED_IN_<version> descriptions and the file to be regenerated and committed.

nodes.name: Runtime patches
nodes.summary: Monkey patches applied from settings.py: graphql-core's executor, ExecutionContext and ExecutionResult, the promise library, asgiref Local and Django database objects.
nodes.detail: patch_executor() wraps complete_value_catching_error so mutation resolvers may use the writer database. The other patches replace __del__ methods to break reference cycles so memory is freed without a full garbage collection (promise issue 106, asgiref issue 487, Django ticket 34865).

nodes.name: validate_query()
nodes.summary: Runs the cost validator, AliasCountLimitRule and MutationCountLimitRule in one graphql-core validation pass and returns the cost with any errors.
nodes.detail: The cost validator is an instance that pretends to be a rule class so the computed cost can be read after validation. All three rules report into the same error list, which the view only enforces when GRAPHQL_QUERY_MAX_COMPLEXITY is non-zero.
nodes.signature: def validate_query(*, schema, document_ast, variables, cost_map)
nodes.code:
error = graphql.validation.validate(
        schema,
        document_ast,
        [
            cost_validator,  # type: ignore[list-item] # cost validator is an instance that pretends to be a class # noqa: E501
            AliasCountLimitRule,
            MutationCountLimitRule,
        ],
    )
    if error:
        return cost_validator.cost, error
    return cost_validator.cost, None

nodes.name: CostValidator
nodes.summary: graphql-core validation rule that walks each operation and sums field complexity, multiplying nested fields by pagination arguments such as first and last from COST_MAP.
nodes.detail: compute_node_cost() recurses through selections and fragments; for each field found in the cost map it multiplies the field's complexity by the product of parent multipliers. Fragment costs on interfaces are merged so the most expensive branch counts. When the total exceeds maximum_cost a QueryCostError is reported with requestedQueryCost and maximumAvailable in its extensions. The cost map is validated against the schema on every operation.
facts: Fields not in the cost map cost 0

nodes.name: AliasCountLimitRule
nodes.summary: Validation rule that counts aliased fields in a document and errors above GRAPHQL_ALIAS_COUNT_LIMIT.

nodes.name: MutationCountLimitRule
nodes.summary: Validation rule that counts top-level mutation fields across operations and errors above GRAPHQL_MUTATION_COUNT_LIMIT.

nodes.name: Query cost map
nodes.summary: COST_MAP: per type and field, a complexity and the argument names (first, last, limit) that multiply the cost of nested selections.
nodes.detail: AGENTS.md requires every new field with a limit argument to be registered here. QUERY_COST_FAILED_OPERATION (1) is the cost recorded for operations that fail before cost analysis.

nodes.name: check_if_query_contains_only_schema()
nodes.summary: Walks operations and fragments to tell introspection-only documents (cacheable) from data queries, and raises when a document mixes both.

nodes.name: Storefront traffic guard
nodes.summary: Implements the shop setting allowStorefrontTraffic: when false, only apps and staff users may call the API directly.
nodes.detail: The flag is cached for 5 minutes in Django's cache under a key namespaced by the current site's primary key, and read from the replica on a miss. ShopSettingsUpdate refreshes the cache when the setting changes. ADR 0006 accepts the propagation delay and ADR 0007 records that introspection and token mutations are blocked too.

nodes.name: is_storefront_traffic_blocked()
nodes.summary: Returns False for apps and when storefront traffic is allowed; otherwise authenticates the user and blocks unless they are staff.
nodes.detail: Checks run cheapest first: request.app is already resolved, the shop flag is cached, and only then is the lazy user resolved, which costs a token decode and a database read.

nodes.name: get_allow_storefront_traffic()
nodes.summary: Reads allow_storefront_traffic from the per-site cache, falling back to SiteSettings on the replica and repopulating the cache.
nodes.code:
def get_allow_storefront_traffic() -> bool:
    cache_key = _get_allow_storefront_traffic_cache_key()
    allow_storefront_traffic = cache.get(cache_key)
    if allow_storefront_traffic is None:
        allow_storefront_traffic = (
            SiteSettings.objects.using(settings.DATABASE_CONNECTION_REPLICA_NAME)
            .values_list("allow_storefront_traffic", flat=True)
            .get(site=Site.objects.get_current())
        )
        set_allow_storefront_traffic_cache(allow_storefront_traffic)
    return allow_storefront_traffic

nodes.name: Upload validation
nodes.summary: Validates uploaded files for fileUpload and media mutations: MIME type against ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES, extension and image content.
nodes.detail: ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES can be extended with the UPLOAD_ADDITIONAL_ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES environment variable (a JSON object).

nodes.name: format_error()
nodes.summary: Formats one error for the response: unwraps the original exception, logs it, masks the message outside DEBUG unless the type is allowed, and adds extensions.exception.code.
nodes.detail: Allowed types include GraphQLError, InvalidTokenError, ValidationError and QueryCostError; anything else becomes 'Internal Server Error' when DEBUG is off. In DEBUG the stack trace is added to the extensions. The current query identifier is attached to the exception for the JSON log formatter.
nodes.code:
# If DEBUG mode is disabled we allow only certain error messages to be returned in
    # the API. This prevents from leaking internals that might be included in Python
    # exceptions' error messages.
    is_allowed_err = type(exc) in ALLOWED_ERRORS or any(
        isinstance(exc, allowed_err) for allowed_err in ALLOWED_ERRORS
    )
    if not is_allowed_err and not settings.DEBUG:
        result["message"] = INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE

nodes.name: GraphQL utilities
nodes.summary: Helpers shared by resolvers and the view: global id resolution, node lookup, requestor from context, query identifier and fingerprint, error formatting and the source-service span tag.
nodes.detail: resolve_global_ids_to_primary_keys() and get_nodes() decode Relay global ids, check the type and load objects in one query. query_identifier() lists sorted root field names; query_fingerprint() adds an MD5 of the document. get_user_or_app_from_context() returns the app when present, else the user. format_error() shapes every error in the response.

nodes.name: Error cleanup
nodes.summary: Converts pydantic errors to Django ValidationError and clears traceback locals on GraphQL errors to break reference cycles created by graphql-core-legacy.
nodes.detail: graphql-core-legacy keeps tracebacks and their frame locals on errors, which ties request objects into reference cycles. clear_errors() walks each error's traceback and clears frame locals after the response is formatted. pydantic_to_validation_error() maps pydantic error locations to Django ValidationError fields with a given code.

nodes.name: PermissionDenied
nodes.summary: Raised by permission checks; its message lists the permissions required so clients see what is missing.

nodes.name: Error code enums
nodes.summary: Enums of error codes returned in typed mutation errors, plus the GraphQL error-type helpers.

nodes.name: Common types and error types
nodes.summary: Error, BulkError and the per-mutation error object types (about 90 classes), plus NonNullList, SecureGlobalID, Permission and display types.
nodes.detail: Each mutation declares its own error_type_class here or in its module, as AGENTS.md requires, so clients can switch on codes per mutation.

nodes.name: get_context_value()
nodes.summary: Turns the Django request into the GraphQL context: dataloader cache, replica flag, request time, calling app, lazy user and decoded token.
nodes.detail: set_app_on_context() loads the app behind an app token only for the API path. set_auth_on_context() sets user to None for apps, else a SimpleLazyObject that runs Django's authenticate() on first access.

nodes.name: clear_context()
nodes.summary: After execution, clears Django field caches on every dataloader value, empties the dataloaders and deletes the user to break reference cycles.

nodes.name: SaleorContext and replica choice
nodes.summary: Defines SaleorContext (the request type resolvers see), the replica switch for mutations and the ChannelContext wrappers.
nodes.detail: disallow_replica_in_context() sets allow_replica False when a mutation starts; get_database_connection_name() returns 'replica' for queries and 'default' for mutations, and code adds .using(name) to querysets. setup_context_user() unwraps the lazy user. ChannelContext and SyncWebhookControlContext carry a node with its channel slug or sync-webhook flag.

nodes.name: get_token_from_request()
nodes.summary: Reads the token from the Authorization-Bearer header, or from Authorization with a JWT or Bearer prefix.

nodes.name: Authentication backends
nodes.summary: Django authentication backends listed in AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS: JSONWebTokenBackend for Saleor tokens and PluginBackend for plugin-provided authentication.
nodes.detail: Permission lookups are cached on the user object. load_user_from_request() applies the shop's password login mode: CUSTOMERS_ONLY strips staff access from first-party tokens and DISABLED rejects them.

nodes.name: JSONWebTokenBackend
nodes.summary: Authenticates a request from a Saleor-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) and computes user and group permissions.

nodes.name: load_user_from_request()
nodes.summary: Decodes a Saleor access token, loads the user by email, checks the user's token key, applies password login mode and narrows permissions to those in the token.
nodes.detail: Third-party access tokens issued for apps and app extensions skip the password login restriction. When the token lists permissions, effective_permissions is replaced by them and is_staff follows.

nodes.name: JSON Web Token helpers
nodes.summary: Creates and decodes Saleor JSON Web Tokens (JWT): access, refresh and third-party access tokens for apps and app extensions.
nodes.detail: Payloads carry type, token key, email and optional permissions; encoding and decoding go through the configured JWT manager. JWT_TTL_ACCESS and JWT_TTL_APP_ACCESS default to 5 minutes, JWT_TTL_REFRESH to 30 days.

nodes.name: JWTManager
nodes.summary: Default JWT manager: loads the RSA private key (optionally password protected), derives the public key and a thumbprint key id, signs RS256 tokens and detached JWS payloads.
nodes.detail: Without RSA_PRIVATE_KEY it raises ImproperlyConfigured unless DEBUG is on, in which case it creates or reuses a 2048-bit key in .jwt_key.pem under PROJECT_ROOT. validate_configuration() runs at start-up from CoreAppConfig. The issuer is the absolute URL of the API route.
facts: The key id is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the public key

nodes.name: JWTManager.decode()
nodes.summary: Verifies RS256 tokens with the public key; tokens whose header names another algorithm are verified as HS256 with SECRET_KEY.
nodes.signature: def decode(cls, token, verify_aud: bool = False)

nodes.name: JWTManager.get_jwks()
nodes.summary: Returns {'keys': [jwk]} for the public key with use 'sig', its key id and alg RS256.

nodes.name: jwt_refresh_token_middleware()
nodes.summary: Django middleware that sets an HttpOnly refresh-token cookie when a mutation left request.refresh_token, expiring with the token.
nodes.detail: The cookie is Secure with SameSite=None outside DEBUG and SameSite=Lax in DEBUG.

nodes.name: one_of_permissions_required()
nodes.summary: Allows the resolver when the requestor holds any of the listed permissions or passes an authorization filter.

nodes.name: Mutation framework
nodes.summary: The base classes every mutation extends: permission checks, writer database switch, typed errors, model create, update, delete and bulk patterns, and event dispatch after commit.
nodes.detail: BaseMutation.mutate() switches the context to the writer database, resolves the user, checks Meta.permissions, then runs perform_mutation() and turns ValidationError into typed errors. DeprecatedModelMutation adds the clean_input, construct_instance, save and post_save_action pipeline for model-backed mutations; ModelDeleteMutation and BaseBulkMutation cover deletes and bulk actions. Webhook and plugin events are sent through call_event(), which defers to transaction.on_commit inside atomic blocks.

nodes.name: Types, connections and dataloaders
nodes.summary: Shared GraphQL building blocks: model object types, scalars and enums, Relay-style cursor connections with pagination limits, filters, and the per-request dataloader base class.
nodes.detail: Connections slice a queryset by a cursor made of the sort fields, fetch one extra row to compute hasNextPage and cap first and last at GRAPHQL_PAGINATION_LIMIT (100). Filter input and the newer where input are applied through django-filter filter sets. DataLoader instances are cached on the request context by context_key, bound to one thread, and read from the replica unless a mutation disabled it.

nodes.name: Metadata API
nodes.summary: The updateMetadata, updatePrivateMetadata, deleteMetadata and deletePrivateMetadata mutations, the ObjectWithMetadata interface and the per-type permission maps.
nodes.detail: Every model with metadata stores public and private JSON columns (ModelWithMetadata). A mutation resolves the global id (or an order or checkout token), looks up the required permissions for the type in PUBLIC_META_PERMISSION_MAP or PRIVATE_META_PERMISSION_MAP, updates the column with a single JSON concatenation UPDATE, and for some types fires a type-specific webhook event such as CHECKOUT_METADATA_UPDATED.

nodes.name: Shop and site settings
nodes.summary: The shop query and the mutations that change site-wide settings, the shop address, gift card, refund and return settings and staff notification recipients, backed by Site and SiteSettings.
nodes.detail: Settings live on SiteSettings, one row per Django Site, reached through get_site_promise() in GraphQL and the patched Site.objects.get_current() elsewhere. Mutations require MANAGE_SETTINGS (gift card settings require MANAGE_GIFT_CARD). ShopSettingsUpdate also updates the storefront traffic cache and fires SHOP_METADATA_UPDATED when metadata changes.

nodes.name: Translations
nodes.summary: Translation queries for staff and the translate mutations for products, variants, media, categories, collections, attributes, pages, menus, shipping, promotions, vouchers and shop settings.
nodes.detail: translations and translation queries need MANAGE_TRANSLATIONS and return TranslatableItem unions. Each translate mutation update_or_creates a row in the model's translations table for a language code inside a traced transaction and emits TRANSLATION_CREATED or TRANSLATION_UPDATED. The mutations are registered by the owning domain's schema (product, attribute, discount, page, menu, shipping, shop).

nodes.name: Settings, database and storage
nodes.summary: settings.py and the runtime plumbing it configures: primary and replica databases, writer-access guards, advisory locks, cache, media storage backends and core app start-up.
nodes.detail: All configuration comes from environment variables read in settings.py. Two database aliases point at the primary and the replica (the same URL unless DATABASE_URL_REPLICA is set). The router sends writes to the primary; reads go to the replica only where code asks for it with .using(). Media goes to S3, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob Storage depending on which bucket variable is set, otherwise to the local file system.

nodes.name: Background jobs and scheduling
nodes.summary: The Celery app, the Celery beat schedule, the custom database scheduler with data-driven schedules, core maintenance tasks, the SQS transport and management commands.
nodes.detail: celeryconf.py builds the Celery app from CELERY_* settings with RestrictWriterDBTask as the base task class and autodiscovers task modules, data migration task packages and plugin tasks. Beat runs saleor.schedulers.schedulers.DatabaseScheduler, which stores entries in django-celery-beat tables and supports custom schedules whose is_due() checks the database, so search-index and checkout-completion tasks only run when rows are marked dirty or ready.

nodes.name: Telemetry, logging and Sentry
nodes.summary: OpenTelemetry tracing and metrics behind replaceable Tracer and Meter classes, GraphQL metrics, JSON logging and Sentry error reporting.
nodes.detail: initialize_telemetry() configures the OpenTelemetry SDK from standard OTEL_* environment variables, enables library instrumentors (psycopg, celery, redis, botocore, threading by default) and initialises the tracer and meter proxies with the classes named in TELEMETRY_TRACER_CLASS and TELEMETRY_METER_CLASS. Sentry is initialised by CoreAppConfig.ready() when SENTRY_DSN is set, with personal data scrubbing.

nodes.name: Shared core utilities
nodes.summary: Domain-neutral helpers used across Saleor: base models with metadata, event payload storage, the hardened HTTP client, EditorJS and HTML cleaning, search parsing, money, weights and anonymisation.
nodes.detail: These modules carry no GraphQL; domain areas import them. The base models define metadata columns with GIN indexes, sortable and publishable models; EventPayload and EventDelivery store webhook payloads and delivery attempts; HTTPClient blocks private IP addresses and redirects for outgoing calls.

nodes.name: Contributor docs and decisions
nodes.summary: README, agent and contributor guides, the security policy, the changelog and the architecture decision records (ADR) in docs/adr.
nodes.detail: AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md is a symbolic link to it) sets the rules the code follows: horizontal scale-out, no reliance on SITE_ID, after-commit scheduling, per-mutation error classes and cost map registration.

nodes.name: Build and deployment files
nodes.summary: Dockerfile, Python project definition, task runner commands, release tooling and the Elastic Beanstalk descriptor.
nodes.detail: The image is a two-stage build: uv installs locked dependencies, the slim runtime image runs collectstatic and starts Uvicorn with 2 workers on port 8000. poe tasks in pyproject.toml start the server, worker and beat scheduler and rebuild schema.graphql.

nodes.name: Base mutation classes
nodes.summary: BaseMutation and its subclasses for model, delete, bulk and channel-restricted mutations, plus FileUpload.
nodes.detail: BaseMutation's metaclass hook requires a description and an error_type_class, validates that permissions is a tuple of enums, appends the permission and webhook event notes to the description and adds the errors field (and a deprecated legacy errors field when error_type_field is set). get_node_or_error() resolves global ids with type checks.

nodes.name: BaseMutation
nodes.summary: The root of every Saleor mutation: Meta options for permissions, error types, metadata support and webhook event docs, and the mutate() template.

nodes.name: BaseMutation.mutate()
nodes.summary: Switches the context to the writer database, resolves the user, enforces permissions and runs perform_mutation(), returning typed errors for ValidationError.
nodes.detail: Decorated with allow_writer() so writes are permitted when the writer-restriction wrappers are active. PermissionDenied propagates as a GraphQL error; ValidationError does not.

nodes.name: BaseMutation.check_permissions()
nodes.summary: Allows the mutation when Meta.permissions is empty, otherwise requires one of them (or all, when asked) via the permission module.

nodes.name: BaseMutation.check_metadata_permissions()
nodes.summary: Looks up the metadata permission function for the object's type, raising NotImplementedError for an unknown type.
nodes.detail: Used by checkoutComplete and orderCreateFromCheckout before they accept metadata input. BaseMetadataMutation.get_permissions() maps each type to its permission function in the same way.

nodes.name: DeprecatedModelMutation
nodes.summary: Model-backed create and update pipeline: get_instance, clean_input, metadata, construct_instance, clean_instance, save, save many-to-many, post_save_action.
nodes.detail: Marked deprecated in its docstring; new mutations are told to extend BaseMutation directly. ModelWithExtRefMutation adds lookup by external reference and ModelWithRestrictedChannelAccessMutation checks the staff user's channel access.

nodes.name: FileUpload
nodes.summary: fileUpload mutation for apps and staff: validates a multipart file, renames it with a random suffix under file_upload/ and saves it to default storage.

nodes.name: call_event()
nodes.summary: Runs a webhook or plugin event function immediately, or on transaction commit when called inside an atomic block.
nodes.detail: This is how AGENTS.md's 'schedule background work after commit' rule is enforced for events; get_is_deferred_payload() in the same file reports whether an event builds its payload later in Celery.

nodes.name: Cursor connections
nodes.summary: Relay-style pagination over querysets and lists: cursors built from sort fields, page info, total count, and filter and where input handling.
nodes.detail: The cursor is a base64 encoded list of the sort field values of the last row. connection_from_queryset_slice() turns it into a keyset filter, takes first or last plus one rows and derives hasNextPage and hasPreviousPage. total_count is a callable so COUNT runs only when the client asks for totalCount. where_filter_qs() supports nested AND and OR (NOT is commented out as a TODO).

nodes.name: connection_from_queryset_slice()
nodes.summary: Builds edges and page info for a queryset from first, last, after and before using a keyset filter on the sort fields.
nodes.signature: def connection_from_queryset_slice(qs, args=None, connection_type=Connection, edge_type=Edge, pageinfo_type=PageInfo)

nodes.name: create_connection_slice()
nodes.summary: Entry point resolvers use: validates first and last, sorts the queryset, slices it with writer access allowed in mutations and wraps nodes in ChannelContext when needed.
nodes.signature: def create_connection_slice(iterable, info, args, connection_type, edge_type=None, pageinfo_type=PageInfo, max_limit=None)

nodes.name: _validate_slice_args()
nodes.summary: Requires first or last when edges are selected and rejects values above the pagination limit (100 by default) with an assertion that the error formatter turns into a GraphQL error.

nodes.name: where_filter_qs()
nodes.summary: Applies the where argument with nested AND and OR operators through the filter set; mixing operators with plain filters is rejected.
nodes.signature: def where_filter_qs(iterable, args, filterset_class, filter_input, request, allow_replica=False)

nodes.name: Field classes
nodes.summary: BaseField (doc category, webhook docs, usage monitoring), PermissionsField (wraps the resolver in a permission check), ConnectionField and FilterConnectionField.
nodes.detail: AGENTS.md asks for PermissionsField to describe field restrictions. FilterConnectionField adds filter, where and sort arguments and applies them before slicing.

nodes.name: PermissionsField
nodes.summary: Field that appends the required permissions to its description and wraps its resolver with one_of_permissions_required.

nodes.name: DataLoader
nodes.summary: Base for every Saleor dataloader: one instance per request per context_key, bound to one thread, reading from the replica or writer chosen by the context, with a tracing span per batch.
nodes.detail: __new__ stores the loader in context.dataloaders so all resolvers in a request share its cache. batch_load_fn() wraps batch_load() in a span recording the row count and allows the writer when the context is a mutation. Resolvers call Loader(info.context).load(key) and get a promise; the promise library batches keys collected in the same tick.

nodes.name: Filter inputs and filter sets
nodes.summary: django-filter based filter sets for the legacy filter argument and the where argument: input object types, range and metadata filters, enum and global id filters.
nodes.detail: FilterInputObjectType generates a GraphQL input from a FilterSet; WhereInputObjectType does the same for where filters with eq, oneOf and range operators. ChannelFilterInputObjectType adds the channel argument.

nodes.name: Shared object types
nodes.summary: Base object, input, enum, connection and interface types, ModelObjectType, money and tax types, upload, events and the order-or-checkout union.
nodes.detail: BaseObjectType carries doc categories and webhook event docs. ModelObjectType ties a graphene type to a Django model and resolves nodes by primary key.

nodes.name: Custom scalars
nodes.summary: Decimal, PositiveDecimal, JSON, Weight, UUID, DateTime, Date and non-negative integer scalars with strict parsing.
facts: enums.py builds enums from Django choices and error code enums
nodes.detail: Decimal and PositiveDecimal parse strings and floats into Python Decimal and reject non-finite values; WeightScalar accepts a number or an object with value and unit and converts to the default weight unit. Enum helpers turn Django choice lists and error code enums into graphene enums.

nodes.name: MetaMutations
nodes.summary: Registers deleteMetadata, deletePrivateMetadata, updateMetadata and updatePrivateMetadata on the root Mutation.

nodes.name: BaseMetadataMutation
nodes.summary: Shared logic for the four metadata mutations: resolve the object from a global id or token, compute permissions from the type's map, update, then run type-specific extra actions.
nodes.detail: get_instance() accepts global ids and, for orders and checkouts, raw ids or tokens; legacy Sale ids are mapped to promotions.

nodes.name: BaseMetadataMutation.mutate()
nodes.summary: Resolves type and primary key, checks the mapped permissions, snapshots old metadata, runs the update and, if anything changed, runs the extra action for the type.

nodes.summary: updateMetadata: merges key-value pairs into an object's public metadata.

nodes.summary: updatePrivateMetadata: merges key-value pairs into an object's private metadata.

nodes.summary: deleteMetadata: removes keys from an object's public metadata.

nodes.name: DeletePrivateMetadata
nodes.summary: deletePrivateMetadata: removes keys from an object's private metadata.

nodes.name: update_metadata()
nodes.summary: Writes metadata with one UPDATE that concatenates the new items onto the JSON column, then refreshes the instance; raises NOT_FOUND when no row was updated.

nodes.name: Metadata permission maps
nodes.summary: PUBLIC_META_PERMISSION_MAP and PRIVATE_META_PERMISSION_MAP: for each GraphQL type name, a function returning the permissions needed to change its metadata.
nodes.detail: Public checkout and checkout line metadata need no permission; private checkout metadata needs MANAGE_CHECKOUTS or HANDLE_TAXES. User and address functions require nothing when the caller owns the object, MANAGE_STAFF for staff users and MANAGE_USERS for customers.

nodes.name: Metadata extra actions
nodes.summary: TYPE_EXTRA_METHODS: per type, the event to fire after metadata changes, for example CHECKOUT_METADATA_UPDATED, ORDER_METADATA_UPDATED or product_metadata_updated.
nodes.detail: When the site uses legacy update webhook emission, checkout and product changes also fire the generic UPDATED event.

nodes.name: ObjectWithMetadata interface
nodes.summary: Interface every metadata-carrying type implements: metadata, metafield, metafields and the private variants, with private reads permission checked.
nodes.detail: metadata, metafield and metafields read the public JSON column and can be filtered by keys; the private variants call check_private_metadata_privilege() first, which maps the model to its GraphQL type and requires the permissions returned by PRIVATE_META_PERMISSION_MAP for that object.

nodes.summary: Abstract Django model with private_metadata and metadata JSON columns, each with a GIN index, and helpers to read, store and delete keys.

nodes.name: Shop type

nodes.summary: The ten mutations under graphql/shop/mutations, all requiring MANAGE_SETTINGS except gift card settings.
nodes.detail: Each loads the current site through get_site_promise(), changes SiteSettings or a related row and returns the Shop object or the changed settings.

nodes.name: ShopSettingsUpdate
nodes.summary: shopSettingsUpdate: changes site-wide settings (header, stock reservation, checkout limits, password login mode, storefront traffic and more) and metadata.
nodes.detail: Rejects restricting password login while the caller is signed in with a password token, validates the customer set-password URL against allowed storefront hosts, normalises stock reservation and quantity limits, saves Site.name separately, saves SiteSettings, refreshes the storefront traffic cache and fires SHOP_METADATA_UPDATED after metadata changes.
nodes.code:
should_update_storefront_traffic_cache = (
            "allow_storefront_traffic" in cleaned_input
        )
        instance = cls.construct_instance(instance, cleaned_input)
        cls.validate_and_update_metadata(
            instance, metadata_collection, private_metadata_collection
        )
        cls.clean_instance(info, instance)
        instance.save()

        if should_update_storefront_traffic_cache:
            # Note: we do not use any locks here as we do not expect any use-case
            #       where this mutation would be called concurrently with different
            #       modes.
            set_allow_storefront_traffic_cache(instance.allow_storefront_traffic)

nodes.name: Patched Site.objects.get_current()
nodes.summary: Replacement for Django's Site.objects.get_current(): finds the site by SITE_ID or request host, caches it in a process-wide dictionary and prefetches settings.
nodes.detail: Loaded by importing site/models.py. The cache is cleared only by clear_cache(), so values can be stale after a save in the same process, as AGENTS.md warns. Lookups use queryset[0], which raises IndexError on a miss, so the 'except Site.DoesNotExist' fallback that strips the port can never run. With the stock SITE_ID = 1 the host branch is not reached at all.

nodes.name: Django settings
nodes.summary: All configuration from environment variables: databases, cache, Celery and beat schedule, storages, JSON Web Token (JWT) keys, GraphQL limits, telemetry, Sentry, plugins, queues and memory limits.
nodes.detail: Applies the runtime monkey patches at import time and sets process memory limits from SOFT_MEMORY_LIMIT_IN_MB and HARD_MEMORY_LIMIT_IN_MB. Built-in plugins are listed in BUILTIN_PLUGINS and external ones are discovered from the saleor.plugins entry point group. ALLOWED_CLIENT_HOSTS must be set when DEBUG is false. Celery tasks run eagerly in-process when CELERY_BROKER_URL is empty.
facts: DB_CONN_MAX_AGE defaults to 0 (close after each request)
An sqs:// broker URL switches CELERY_BROKER_TRANSPORT to saleor.core.sqs.Transport
DEBUG defaults to true when unset; SITE_ID is fixed at 1

nodes.name: CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE
nodes.summary: Periodic tasks: cleanups, promotion toggles, search vector updates, order expiry, app removal, fund release, price recalculation and automatic checkout completion.
nodes.detail: Fixed entries use timedelta or crontab; promotion toggles, search updates and checkout completion use custom schedules from core/schedules.py. Price recalculation runs every BEAT_PRICE_RECALCULATION_SCHEDULE (30 seconds) with a matching expiry. When OBSERVABILITY_BROKER_URL is set an observability-reporter entry is added.

nodes.name: SENTRY_INIT()
nodes.summary: Initialises the Sentry software development kit with Django and Celery integrations, the Saleor release and a recursive scrubber for private metadata and personal fields.

nodes.name: PrimaryReplicaRouter
nodes.summary: Database router that sends every write to the default (primary) connection and allows all relations; it defines no read routing, so reads use the replica only through explicit .using().

nodes.name: Writer access guards
nodes.summary: Context managers and wrappers that detect accidental use of the writer database: allow_writer(), restrict_writer (raises) and log_writer_usage (logs with a stack trace).
nodes.detail: ENABLE_RESTRICT_WRITER_MIDDLEWARE adds the logging middleware, not the raising one; tests use restrict_writer_middleware. Celery tasks apply CELERY_RESTRICT_WRITER_METHOD through RestrictWriterDBTask.

nodes.name: log_writer_usage()
nodes.summary: Database execute wrapper that logs a warning with a stack trace when the writer is used outside allow_writer().
nodes.signature: def log_writer_usage(execute, sql, params, many, context)

nodes.name: Advisory locks
nodes.summary: Transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory locks with a configurable namespace; used to serialise category and menu item tree writes (ADR 0009).
nodes.detail: acquire_advisory_xact_lock() must run inside an atomic block and calls pg_advisory_xact_lock(namespace, key). The namespace defaults to 21218 and can come from ADVISORY_LOCK_NAMESPACE_IMPORT.

nodes.name: Database expressions and fields
nodes.summary: PostgresJsonConcatenate for in-place JSON updates, sanitised JSON and money fields, and the ilike lookup.
nodes.detail: PostgresJsonConcatenate renders the PostgreSQL || operator so metadata writes merge keys inside one UPDATE. SanitizedJSONField cleans values on save; MoneyField and TaxedMoneyField compose amount and currency columns into prices objects. postgres.py adds search vector expressions that skip Django's validation for speed.

nodes.name: Media storage backends
nodes.summary: django-storages subclasses for public and private media on Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob Storage, each taking its bucket or container from settings.
nodes.detail: Private storage classes clear the custom domain (S3) or custom endpoint (Google Cloud Storage), so private files are not addressed through a public host.

nodes.name: CoreAppConfig
nodes.summary: Start-up hook: registers the ilike lookup, initialises Sentry when SENTRY_DSN is set, validates the JWT manager and advisory lock namespace, and sets Pillow's pixel limit.
nodes.detail: Pillow's limit is set to half of MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS because Pillow only raises above twice its limit.

nodes.name: Celery app
nodes.summary: Creates the Celery app 'saleor' configured from CELERY_* settings, with RestrictWriterDBTask as the default task class, and autodiscovers task modules.
nodes.detail: Also discovers data-migration task packages per release (saleor3_20 to saleor3_23), plugin modules and search_tasks modules. Worker processes initialise telemetry on fork; Celery's own logging setup is skipped in favour of Django's.

nodes.name: Data-driven beat schedules
nodes.summary: Custom Celery schedules whose is_due() asks the database: promotion start and end times, rows marked search_index_dirty, and checkouts ready for automatic completion.
nodes.detail: Each schedule is a module-level instance referenced by import path so the database scheduler can rebuild it. The search and completion schedules check every 60 seconds on the replica and run only when work exists. The promotion schedule sleeps until the next start or end date (at most 60 seconds) and switches to 5-second batches when more promotions than the batch size are pending.
facts: initial_timedelta is 60 seconds for every schedule
BEAT_UPDATE_SEARCH_FREQUENCY only sets task expiry, not the 60-second check

nodes.name: TimeBaseSchedule
nodes.summary: Base schedule that is due when are_dirty() returns True and asks beat to check again after the remaining interval or the initial 60 seconds.
nodes.code:
def is_due(self, last_run_at):
        """Return tuple of ``(is_due, next_time_to_run)``.

        Note:
            Next time to run is in seconds.

        """
        last_run_at = self.maybe_make_aware(last_run_at)
        rem_delta = self.remaining_estimate(last_run_at)
        remaining_s = max(rem_delta.total_seconds(), 0)
        if remaining_s == 0:
            remaining_s = self.initial_timedelta.total_seconds()

        are_marked_as_dirty = self.are_dirty()
        return schedstate(is_due=are_marked_as_dirty, next=remaining_s)

nodes.name: product_search_update_schedule
nodes.summary: Due when any product has search_index_dirty=True on the replica; drives update_products_search_vector_task. Sibling classes do the same for pages, gift cards and checkouts.

nodes.name: checkout_automatic_completion_schedule
nodes.summary: Due when a channel with automatic completion has a fully authorised checkout with an email or user and billing address, older than the channel's delay and newer than the oldest allowed change.

nodes.name: Beat schedulers
nodes.summary: Celery beat schedulers with a rewritten tick(): DatabaseScheduler (django-celery-beat tables) and PersistentScheduler (shelve file).
nodes.detail: pyproject's scheduler task starts beat with DatabaseScheduler. CustomModelEntry adds the 'custom' schedule type stored in CustomSchedule rows.

nodes.name: BaseScheduler.tick()
nodes.summary: Rewritten beat loop: walks the heap from the end, calls is_due() only for entries whose time has come, applies due entries and returns the shortest wait, capped at max_interval.
nodes.detail: Fixes two Celery behaviours documented in its docstring: waiting longer than the earliest entry, and getting stuck on an entry whose is_due() keeps returning False.
nodes.signature: def tick(self, event_t=HeapEventType, min=min, heappop=None, heappush=None)

nodes.name: DatabaseScheduler
nodes.summary: Beat scheduler backed by the database through django-celery-beat, using CustomPeriodicTask so entries can carry custom schedules.

nodes.name: CustomSchedule model
nodes.summary: Row holding the import path of a custom schedule instance; schedule imports it and caches it in CACHED_SCHEDULES.
nodes.detail: The cache is read by schedule_import_path but written under the module path, so the lookup always misses and the import runs every time.

nodes.name: RestrictWriterDBTask
nodes.summary: Base Celery task that wraps every run in the database execute wrapper named by CELERY_RESTRICT_WRITER_METHOD, logging (production) or raising (tests) on unexpected writer use.

nodes.name: delete_event_payloads_task()
nodes.summary: Daily task that deletes webhook event payloads no longer referenced by a recent delivery, in batches, re-queuing itself until done or out of time.
nodes.detail: Payloads with no delivery created within EVENT_PAYLOAD_DELETE_PERIOD (14 days) are selected on the replica, deleted on the writer and their files removed from private storage by a follow-up task. The chain stops when EVENT_PAYLOAD_DELETE_TASK_TIME_LIMIT (1 hour) has passed.

nodes.name: SQS channel
nodes.summary: Kombu Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) channel that forwards message attributes and MessageGroupId (also on retries), adds FIFO deduplication ids and maps ETA to DelaySeconds up to 900.
nodes.detail: Used when CELERY_BROKER_URL starts with sqs://. The retry fix works around kombu issue 2400, where Task.retry() drops custom properties.
facts: DelaySeconds is capped at 900, the SQS maximum

nodes.name: Management commands
nodes.summary: Operator and developer commands: populatedb, cleardb, clearorders, update_search_indexes, delete_event_payloads, generate_json_schemas, check_mptt_trees and more.
nodes.detail: populatedb fills a development database with sample catalogue, orders and users from core/development/random_data.py. generate_json_schemas writes the synchronous webhook response schemas into saleor/json_schemas. check_mptt_trees detects corrupted category and menu trees; remove_invalid_files deletes stored files with dangerous MIME types.

nodes.name: initialize_telemetry()
nodes.summary: Configures the OpenTelemetry SDK from OTEL_* variables, enables the instrumentors in TELEMETRY_INSTRUMENTORS and initialises the tracer and meter proxies.
nodes.detail: Called lazily after fork by Uvicorn preload and Celery worker start so each process owns its exporters. Library instrumentors get a no-op meter provider so only Saleor's own metrics are exported.

nodes.name: Tracer
nodes.summary: Replaceable tracing interface over OpenTelemetry with CORE and SERVICE scopes, context extraction and injection, and spans enriched with global attributes.

nodes.name: Meter
nodes.summary: Replaceable metrics interface over OpenTelemetry that creates counters and histograms once, with unit conversion and duplicate checks.

nodes.name: GraphQL metrics
nodes.summary: Defines and records GraphQL metrics: operation count, duration and cost, slow operations, field usage, request count and duration, batch size, alias and mutation counts.
nodes.detail: Instruments are created on the SERVICE meter at import. Slow operations above TELEMETRY_SLOW_GRAPHQL_OPERATION_THRESHOLD (1 second) are also recorded in a separate histogram.
facts: Metric names start with saleor.graphql. or saleor.request.

nodes.name: JSON log formatters
nodes.summary: JSON formatters for Django, Celery and Celery task logs adding hostname, level, the failing GraphQL query and task id and name.
nodes.detail: JsonFormatter adds hostname and level and, for GraphQL errors, the query identifier stored on the exception by format_error() along with the Saleor version. The Celery formatters add the task id, name and runtime from the log record or the current task.

nodes.name: Core base models
nodes.summary: Abstract SortableModel, PublishableModel, ModelWithMetadata and ModelWithExternalReference, plus Job, EventPayload, EventDelivery and EventDeliveryAttempt tables.
nodes.detail: SortableModel keeps a sort_order and renumbers siblings on delete; PublishableModel adds is_published and a published() queryset filter. ModelWithMetadata adds two JSON columns with GIN indexes. EventPayload, EventDelivery and EventDeliveryAttempt are the storage behind webhook delivery and its retries; Job is a status record for asynchronous jobs.

nodes.name: EventPayload
nodes.summary: Stored webhook payload, either inline text or a file in private storage, shared by the deliveries that send it.

nodes.name: HTTPClient
nodes.summary: requests-hardened manager used for outgoing calls: blocks private and loopback IP addresses (HTTP_IP_FILTER_ENABLED), never follows redirects, sets a Saleor user agent and the common timeout.

nodes.name: EditorJS cleaning
nodes.summary: Pydantic models of EditorJS blocks and a cleaner that validates rich text JSON, sanitises HTML in text and cleans URLs before it is stored.
nodes.detail: clean_editorjs() parses the document with strict block models, then dumps it back; editorjs_to_text() extracts plain text for search. Link rel and allowed attributes come from EDITOR_JS_* variables via HtmlCleanerSettings.

nodes.name: Search query parsing
nodes.summary: Turns a websearch-style string (words, OR, negation, quoted phrases) into a PostgreSQL tsquery with prefix matching and ranks exact matches first.
nodes.detail: The input is tokenised into words, OR operators, negations and quoted phrases; words become prefix terms (word:*), phrases become followed-by chains and negations are prefixed with !. prefix_search() applies the resulting tsquery to a queryset's search vector and orders exact matches ahead of prefix matches.

nodes.name: Core utilities
nodes.summary: Domain and public URL helpers, absolute URI building, client IP extraction from REAL_IP_ENVIRON, unique slug generation and file download into storage.
nodes.detail: build_absolute_uri() combines PUBLIC_URL (or the current site domain and ENABLE_SSL) with a path. get_client_ip() reads the headers named in REAL_IP_ENVIRON and validates IPv4 or IPv6. generate_unique_slug() appends a number until the slug is free. Also folds in anonymisation fakes and notification helpers.

nodes.name: URL validation
nodes.summary: validate_storefront_url() accepts only hosts in ALLOWED_CLIENT_HOSTS; also builds redirect URLs and sanitises URLs for logs.
nodes.detail: validate_storefront_url() parses the URL and accepts it only if its host matches ALLOWED_CLIENT_HOSTS, preventing redirects to arbitrary hosts from password reset and similar links. sanitize_url_for_logging() masks credentials and can strip query strings and fragments before URLs are logged.

nodes.name: Money, weight and units
nodes.summary: Price quantisation, weight conversion, measurement unit enums, tax error types and the payment and pricing interfaces shared by plugins.
nodes.detail: quantize_price() rounds money to the currency's precision. Weight helpers convert between units with the measurement library. PaymentInterface and the pricing LineInfo describe what payment and discount code expects from plugins; languages.py lists the language codes accepted by translations.

nodes.name: Webhook response JSON schemas
nodes.summary: Generated JSON Schema files describing what apps must return to synchronous webhooks such as CheckoutCalculateTaxes, TransactionChargeRequested and ShippingListMethodsForCheckout.

nodes.name: README
nodes.summary: Project overview: an API-only, GraphQL-native commerce platform, with links to documentation, demo, community and installation guides.

nodes.name: Agent and contributor rules
nodes.summary: Rules for code changes: scale-out deployment model, per-site resolution, API versioning annotations, no Django signals, concurrency patterns, data migrations and test style.
nodes.detail: CLAUDE.md is a symbolic link to this file.

nodes.name: GraphQL layer rules
nodes.summary: GraphQL rules: one error class per mutation, ADDED_IN version tags, 100-item input limits and cost map registration for limited fields.

nodes.name: Changelog
nodes.summary: Unreleased changes for 3.24, led by breaking changes such as round-up thumbnail sizes, removed payment plugins and bulk delete limits.

nodes.name: Architecture decision records
nodes.summary: Twelve short decision records on gift cards, assignment, balance adjustments, storefront traffic blocking, webhook identifiers, tree locks, payment history, deferred payloads and thumbnail rounding.
nodes.detail: Two files share the number 0011 (deferred webhook payloads and thumbnail rounding).

nodes.name: Container image
nodes.summary: Two-stage image: uv sync of locked dependencies on python:3.12, then a slim runtime with image and SQS libraries, a non-root saleor user, collectstatic and Uvicorn on port 8000.
facts: Keep-alive timeout 35 seconds, graceful shutdown 30 seconds

flows.name: A GraphQL request, from HTTP to resolver and back
flows.summary: How one POST /graphql/ is parsed, limited, authenticated, permission checked, executed and returned.

steps.text: A storefront, the dashboard or an app POSTs a JSON body with query, variables and operationName to /graphql/.
Uvicorn hands the request to the ASGI stack: health check shortcut, gzip, CORS headers and telemetry attributes wrap Django's handler.
Django's URL table routes ^graphql/$ to GraphQLView with CSRF checks disabled.
handle_query() opens a server span and request metrics; _handle_query() parses the body and rejects batches above GRAPHQL_BATCH_MAX_COUNT.
The cached backend parses the document and runs the standard validation rules once per distinct query string, keeping 1000 documents.
The view rejects introspection mixed with data queries and any subscription operation, then labels the span with the query identifier and fingerprint.
Cost, alias and mutation count rules run together. With GRAPHQL_QUERY_MAX_COMPLEXITY set (default 50000), any error returns 400 with the cost in extensions.
The request becomes the context: dataloader cache, replica flag, the app behind an app token and a lazy user decoded from a JSON Web Token.
If the shop disabled storefront traffic, anonymous and customer requests stop here with 401; apps and staff continue.
For a mutation, the context switches to the writer database, the user is resolved and Meta.permissions are checked; queries use PermissionsField decorators instead.
The resolver or mutation class does the work, for example checkoutComplete, loading related rows through request-scoped dataloaders.
Dataloaders batch lookups per request and read from the replica for queries and the writer for mutations.
Errors are formatted (internal messages masked outside DEBUG), data and extensions assembled, and the status set to 200, 400 or 401.
Each error carries extensions.exception.code; unexpected exceptions are logged at error level by the saleor.graphql.errors.unhandled logger.

flows.name: A background job, from Celery beat to a task
flows.summary: How the beat scheduler decides a data-driven entry is due and a worker runs the task.

steps.text: settings.py lists periodic entries; update-products-search-vectors uses the custom product_search_update_schedule instead of a fixed interval.
Beat runs with DatabaseScheduler (poe scheduler), which syncs entries into django-celery-beat tables as CustomPeriodicTask rows.
The rewritten tick() checks each entry whose time has come and sleeps for the shortest remaining wait, at most 300 seconds.
is_due() asks the replica whether any product has search_index_dirty=True and asks to be checked again in 60 seconds.
When due, beat publishes update_products_search_vector_task to the broker (Redis, RabbitMQ or SQS through the custom channel).
A worker started from celeryconf.py picks the message up; telemetry was initialised when the worker process forked.
The base task class wraps the run so unexpected queries on the writer database are logged.
The catalog task rebuilds search vectors for a batch of dirty products and clears the flag; its expiry comes from BEAT_UPDATE_SEARCH_EXPIRE_AFTER_SEC.

flows.name: Updating metadata on any object
flows.summary: How updateMetadata finds the object, picks the right permission, writes JSON in one query and fires a webhook.

steps.text: updateMetadata is one of four generic metadata mutations on the root Mutation.
The id is decoded to a type and primary key; orders and checkouts may also be addressed by raw id or token.
The type name selects a permission function from PUBLIC_META_PERMISSION_MAP, for example MANAGE_PRODUCTS for products or none for checkouts.
After the permission check, perform_mutation() validates keys and calls update_metadata().
One UPDATE concatenates the new keys onto the JSON column, avoiding a read-modify-write race.
If metadata changed, the type's extra action fires its event, such as PRODUCT_METADATA_UPDATED, through the plugin and webhook manager.
